short: Statutory health and disability insurance for lower-wage employees.
seoTitle: ESI — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: Statutory health and disability insurance for lower-wage employees. Missing coverage for eligible staff is a compliance exposure that grows quietly.
definition: Employees' State Insurance is a statutory scheme providing medical care, sickness benefit and related cover to employees earning below a wage ceiling, funded by contributions from both employer and employee.
bodyHtml:
Why ESI matters

ESI applicability is driven by both establishment size and individual wages, so it changes as pay rises. Missing coverage for eligible staff is a compliance exposure that grows quietly.

How ESI works in practice

Check applicability whenever wages are revised, since an employee can move out of coverage mid-year. Contributions are deposited monthly with a return, on the same discipline as provident fund.

faq.question: Who is covered by ESI?
faq.answer: Employees earning up to the prescribed wage ceiling in covered establishments; the ceiling is revised from time to time.

faq.question: What does ESI provide?
faq.answer: Medical treatment for the employee and dependants, plus sickness, maternity and disability benefits.
